prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals and commitments

- Economy and tax: Reduce waste by £12bn a year by 2007–08; use £8bn to cut borrowing and £4bn for tax reductions in the first Budget. Increase overall public spending by 4% a year to 2011–12. Maintain or increase funding for the NHS, schools, transport and international development; increase spending on police, defence and pensions. Halve council tax bills for households where all residents are over 65 (up to £500, funded centrally). Link the basic state pension to earnings; retain existing pensioner benefits. Create Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; strengthen workplace pensions with opt-out auto-enrolment and use unclaimed assets to support those losing out from scheme failures. Keep Bank of England independence; do not join the euro. Cut regulation via departmental regulatory budgets, sunset reviews and ending “gold-plating.” Seek to restore opt-out from EU employment rules affecting small firms.

- Families, childcare and education: Offer flexible maternity pay (six or nine months). Provide up to £50 per week per under‑5 child for qualifying working families, usable with formal or informal childcare; support workplace nurseries and new after‑school clubs. Increase school funding by £15bn a year by 2009–10. Strengthen school discipline by giving heads control over admissions and expulsions; create Turnaround Schools; reduce teacher paperwork; simplify funding so money follows the pupil. Reform exams (publish marks with grades, allow international qualifications), slim the National Curriculum, and ban junk food in schools; guarantee two hours of after‑school sport. Expand parental choice with 600,000 additional places in the first term; allow good schools to grow and permit access to independent schools at or below state cost. Place a moratorium on closing special schools and improve SEND choice. Reform further education funding and allow “super college” status. Abolish university tuition fees and the admissions regulator; support university endowments.

- Health and social care: Increase NHS spending by £34bn over the Parliament; reduce administrative tiers (fewer PCTs, abolish SHAs and some quangos); end central targets; expand hospital autonomy. Reintroduce matrons with authority on cleanliness; fund infection control; expand single rooms. Give patients and GPs choice of provider; fund services per patient treated; protect community hospitals. Contribute toward costs when patients self‑fund operations (up to half the NHS equivalent). Reform social care so no one is forced to sell their home; expand respite for carers. Improve NHS dentistry access with revised payments and low monthly coverage plans. Health checks for non‑EU migrants staying over 12 months. Launch an STI public health campaign.

- Crime and justice: Recruit 5,000 additional police officers annually; reduce paperwork; introduce elected police commissioners. End early release; add 20,000 prison places; require transparency on minimum time served. Expand drug treatment, including 25,000 residential rehab places; reclassify cannabis to class B. Enhance counter‑terror coordination, laws, resourcing and training.

- Immigration and borders: Create a unified Border Control Police; restore embarkation checks; 24‑hour port surveillance. Introduce a points‑based work permit system. Process asylum applications outside the UK; take a fixed annual quota of UNHCR refugees; set an overall annual migration limit approved by Parliament; seek relevant powers back from EU and update treaty commitments.

- Governance and devolution: Publish a delivery timetable; abolish regional assemblies and return powers to local authorities. Strengthen parliamentary scrutiny; reduce MPs by 20%; seek a substantially elected upper chamber. Ensure “English votes for English laws.” In Wales, hold a referendum on the Assembly’s future powers; uphold consent-based principles in Northern Ireland with conditions for executive participation.

- Communities, housing, transport, environment: Devolve powers to councils; strengthen planning enforcement (including on illegal encampments); devolve arts and lottery decisions. Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership. Modernise roads; review speed cameras; grant longer rail franchises. Protect green belts; prioritise brownfield development. Phase out HFCs; incentivise home energy efficiency; cut VED and increase grants for low‑emission cars; expand recycling; support renewable energy and efficiency for security of supply.

- Rural and agriculture: Free vote on repealing the hunting ban. Tighten honest food labelling; reduce farm regulation; require public procurement to meet “Little Red Tractor” standards; pursue CAP reform; update animal welfare laws.

- Defence and foreign policy: Increase frontline defence spending by £2.7bn by 2007–08; support service families; retain regimental structures; improve procurement; keep NATO central. Remain engaged in Iraq’s reconstruction; support a two‑state solution in the Middle East. Hold a referendum on the EU Constitution within six months and campaign against it; do not join the euro; seek opt‑outs and national control over fisheries; support further EU enlargement, including Turkey. Move towards 0.7% of national income for aid by 2013; support debt relief; increase national control over aid spending.

- First‑month actions: Begin recruiting extra police; reintroduce matrons; present a first Budget implementing savings and tax measures; give head teachers expulsion powers; start 24‑hour port surveillance; set the EU Constitution referendum date.
